title: Method C Out-of-Sample Holdout Comparative Synthesis (Increments 85 vs 88)
summary: Evaluation of localized AT2 phase-field discretization sharpening model across two progressive holdout increments.

synthesis_findings.error_trend_with_displacement: Residual r_E shifted from -0.209% at Inc 85 (u = 0.001912 mm) to -0.466% at Inc 88 (u = 0.001965 mm). Negative bias deepened by 0.257 percentage points as displacement increased.
synthesis_findings.error_trend_with_damage: As receiver peak damage progressed from d_max = 0.594 (Inc 85) to d_max = 0.730 (Inc 88), the physical system entered active localized crack-softening on Candidate C4, increasing continuous within-step relaxation and reducing stored elastic strain energy.
synthesis_findings.stationarity_divergence: While Increment 85 achieved stationary equilibrium in 10 cycles (Delta d = 0.0008 <= 0.001), Increment 88 reached the 15-cycle loop cap without stationarity (Delta d = 0.0072, Delta RF2 = 0.438 N). This proves that static alternating minimization at fixed displacement cannot achieve rapid stationarity once localized damage exceeds ~0.70.
synthesis_findings.domain_of_applicability: The localized linear crack-tip variational sharpening model is predictive for pre-localization states (d_max <= 0.60, r_E in [-0.21%, +0.05%]), but underestimates relaxation as damage localization transitions into crack growth (d_max >= 0.70).
synthesis_findings.statistical_limitation: Increments 85 and 88 share the identical coarse donor trajectory and fine C4 mesh. They represent correlated progressive validation points along one trajectory, not independent random samples.
